text:
Seattle University adds Ladji Coulibaly to men's basketball roster for 2026-27
Seattle University men's basketball announced the addition of Ladji Coulibaly, a 6-foot-10 center from Kati, Mali, to the Redhawks' roster for the 2026-27 season on Aug. 19.
Head coach Chris Victor said, "Ladji brings size, athleticism and a wealth of experience to our frontcourt. He has developed in some outstanding basketball environments, from the NBA Global Academy and Centre of Excellence to BAXI Manresa, junior college and international competition with Mali. That experience, along with his ability to rebound, finish around the basket and impact the game defensively, will be a great addition to our program."
Coulibaly joins Seattle U after playing his freshman season at New Mexico Junior College. During that season he appeared in 34 games and averaged 7.9 points and 7.1 rebounds per game while shooting 56.5 percent from the field. He helped lead New Mexico JC to a 27-7 record in the 2025-26 season—the most wins for the program since 2014—and an appearance in the Round of 16 at the NJCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship.
Before attending New Mexico JC, Coulibaly was part of both the NBA Global Academy and Centre of Excellence in Canberra, Australia. He also played for BAXI Manresa club in Spain's ACB League.
Coulibaly brings international experience as well; he has represented Mali at several FIBA youth world and continental competitions, including participation in events such as the 2021 FIBA U16 African Championship—where Mali finished as runner-up—the 2022 FIBA U17 Basketball World Cup, and most recently at the 2025 FIBA U19 Basketball World Cup.
Victor said Coulibaly's background would contribute significantly on both ends of the court as Seattle University prepares for its upcoming season.
